cases.input: A treatment trace is from a newer bundle and a different route configuration than the control. Its custom ready event is 18% earlier.
required: Define the custom readiness metric and required visible state.
Mark the comparison unmatched and reject a causal claim.
Request same-build control and treatment runs that differ only in the intended switch.
reject: Call the treatment an 18% causal improvement.

cases.input: A workbook combines ten run rows, two failed runs, a median row and a notes footer. A proposed script averages the numeric column and drops the failures.
required: Separate run rows from summaries and footer content.
Preserve failed runs and candidate identity.
Report medians and a distribution with explicit exclusion rules.
reject: Delete outliers because they weaken the result.

cases.input: A new preload uses a handcrafted URL and cache key. The normal consumer later calls the production request helper with timezone and filter options, causing a second request.
required: Distinguish discovery, download, evaluation and initialization.
Compare exact request and cache identity.
Reuse the production helper and preserve timezone, filter, retry and error semantics.
reject: Keep a parallel cache for the preload.
Claim earlier request start proves critical-path improvement.

cases.input: Optional initialization is moved into an async animation-frame callback because the author expects code after await to run after the next paint.
required: Identify the Promise continuation as a pre-paint microtask in the usual event-loop ordering.
Use and verify a frame-followed-by-task strategy if a true post-paint continuation is required.
Test control, treatment, ineligible and cancellation/navigation paths.
reject: Treat an async RAF callback as proof of post-paint execution.

cases.input: A default-off treatment improves a custom readiness median but starts a long initialization task immediately afterward. LCP becomes later and the LCP candidate repaints.
required: Inspect LCP candidate identity and repaint timing.
Relate the long task to the paint timeline without conflating readiness and LCP.
Report the readiness improvement and LCP regression as a tradeoff rather than one net win.
reject: Declare success using only the custom readiness metric.
Hide the LCP result as an outlier.

cases.input: A startup change passes on one client-rendered route. Configuration also supports server rendering, compact headers, prerendering and alternate child layouts, but the proposal assumes they behave identically.
required: Inventory variants from authoritative routing and configuration.
Build a scenario matrix including OFF, ON and ineligible behavior.
Cover hidden documents, navigation and stale/race paths where applicable.
reject: Infer all variants from the tested route.

cases.input: A trace contains a slow optional-module evaluation. Readiness does not await it, but it overlaps a data request that is the last readiness prerequisite.
required: Determine whether the optional work is blocking, contending, concurrent or fallback behavior.
Identify the last readiness prerequisite.
Test whether shifting the optional work changes the critical prerequisite or only resource contention.
reject: Optimize the longest trace bar without tracing readiness dependencies.

cases.input: One product wants optional content to initialize after primary paint. A proposal adds product policy and a reverse import to a generic loader used by many products.
required: Keep product-specific timing at the experience or consumer boundary.
Reserve the generic loader for cross-product mechanics.
Check exact runtime/import edges and prefer injection or a pure module over a new cycle.
reject: Add the reverse import because broad dependency diagnostics already have unrelated failures.

cases.input: Matched local runs show the treatment unchanged, while several runs fail because an external test dependency is unavailable. An unrelated baseline test also fails on control.
required: Attribute the external blocker and pre-existing baseline failure separately.
Do not patch the baseline or broaden the optimization.
Limit performance claims to the matched evidence actually obtained.
reject: Change unrelated tests to produce a green run.
Report the unavailable dependency as treatment success.
